prompt:
You are watching a volleyball match from a fixed camera.

This clip begins at {start} seconds into the match.
Note: Clips are short and often start in the middle of an ongoing rally. If the ball is already in play when the clip begins, DO NOT guess a 'serve' or 'receive' for that rally.

List ball contacts you see DURING LIVE PLAY ONLY. Ignore all dead-time contacts (e.g., players celebrating, passing the ball back, or warming up between rallies).

Rules for types:
- serve: One team tosses the ball and hits it over the net from out of bounds behind the baseline to start a point. A rally has exactly ONE serve. Never report a serve if the ball is already in play, and ignore practice tosses.
- receive: The opposing team's first contact passing the serve. Usually a forearm pass inside the court. A rally has exactly ONE receive. Do not report receives mid-rally.
- dig: A defensive pass saving an opponent's attack.
- set: An overhead pass setting up an attack. DEFINITIONAL RULE: The scout only records sets that lead to a kill. ONLY report a 'set' if the VERY NEXT contact is a 'kill'. If it leads to a normal 'attack' or 'dig', DO NOT report the set.
- attack: An offensive hit directing the ball across the net.
- kill: An attack that immediately scores a point. Report the attacker's hit as a 'kill'. Do not report the defender's failed touch as a 'dig'.
- block: A defensive jump at the net intercepting an opponent's attack.

For each contact give:
  t       - time of contact in absolute match seconds
  type    - serve, receive, dig, set, attack, kill or block
  side    - "left" or "right": which half of the frame the player is in
  number  - jersey number as a string, or null
  error   - true if the contact was a mistake
  point   - true if the rally ended here
